To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stable polymers with free electrons can be obtained by polymerization of monoradicals and that these polymers can be used as spin-labels for the investigation of the mobility and the entanglement of macromolecules.

(a) stable polymers with one or more unpaired electrons can be prepared; (b) these polymers are characterized by their EPR spectrum; (c) stable polymers are of great interest for the preparation of graft copolymers; (d) the mobility of polymers can be determined by spin labelling; (e) stable polymers can be used for the preparation of conducting polymers.

stable polyradicals are a new class of materials that can be synthesized by various methods, that their properties can be tuned by the choice of the monomer and that they are of great use for the characterization of the mobility of polymers.

the synthesis of stable polymers and their use as initiators in polymerizations.
the synthesis, properties and reactions as well as the applications of stable polymers containing unpaired electrons.
the synthesis of polyradicals, their properties and their use as initiators for the grafting of polymeric chains on to other polymer backbones.

stable polymers with free radicals are of interest for the synthesis of new polymers and for the characterization of polymers.
stable polymers with an unpaired electron have a great potential for future use in materials science.
